I remember playing this a long time ago in its beta stage, back when it was solely browser based. Although things may have changed since then, here are some the things I remember.

I remember that the paid sections (treasure hunts) and f2p extra chest is in no required nor did they give any undue advantage. You will gain the most advantage from the f2p extra chest early on, starting at the level 3 modules. This is because you don't have a lot of equipment in which to develop strategies. The remaining paid sections are purely cosmetic.

important
First and foremost don't sell any equipment unless you have more than, say, three duplicates. Different modules will require different strategies. These strategies come from combining specific card abilities that are attached to the variety of equipment. Simply amassing the hardest hitting damage cards will not lead to success in every case. Some modules will require armour penetration, others will require mobility. Keep even the lowly level 1 equipment as they can come in handy. There is no disadvantage in keeping all the equipment you gain. Sell only the treasures, unless you want to start a collection. Save your gold to buy exceptional equipment rather than more basic equipment.

Nominally, it combines a grid-based adventure map and elements of a deck-builder. Unlike other deck builder games, you don't build the deck up card by card. You equip your characters with various weapons and armour of which each piece has a preset selection of cards. The size of your deck increases with the levels you gain that unlock equipment slots. Once you get higher in level you will begin to acquire equipment with "power tokens". Each character will unlock "power token" slots as they level up which forces you to juggle which pieces of your powerful equipment you want to incorporate into your strategy. Some of the cards have detrimental effects on your character.

I suggest that new players dip into the PvP Arena section of the game when you are able. Be aware that you will probably get clobbered after you raise your ranking a bit. Do not fret. Higher end PvP is tailored to characters of at least level 15 with a large variety of equipment and strategy options. All characters will be level 15 in PvP no matter what the character's true level is and you have access to your stash of equipment. There are multiple reasons I suggest PvP. First and foremost, each match you win will reward you with a chest of loot. After winning a couple of matches in a day you will be rewarded with a rare chest that has at least one rare or better item. The equipment rewards in PvP are less restrictive so it is quite possible to get equipment that is higher level than what you could acquire at the time in PvE.

If you have the time, go back to previous modules each day to gain even more equipment. At best you can get your hands on rare, epic and legendary equipment, especially those of level 1-6 that don't have power tokens attached to them. At worst you get your hands on excess duplicates and extra treasure in which to sell which will get you closer to being able to buy a choice item in one of the shops.

One note about buying items from the shops is that the price of equipment in the shops will have a price multiplier. If the equipment is higher in level than your character it will be more expensive than if you were closer in level to it. I don't remember if lower level equipment being sold has a fraction of the base price taken off.

There is also a wiki with a lot of information if you so desire. http://wiki.cardhuntria.com/wiki/Cardhuntria:Community_portal
Wow, that's a lot of interesting points you covered :) Thank you for the tips on playing online.

As I mentioned before, many more strategic options can be developed once you get into the game some more and collect a larger variety of equipment. If you plan on playing a lot of modules per day then I definitely suggest hopping into (pizza) paid section "The Card Hunter Club". It is in that part that gets you the extra item at the completion of the modules and PvP matches. To quote the text on it, "Your Club Reward item will be at least as rare as the rarest item you would otherwise be guaranteed. For example, if you open a chest containing a guaranteed epic item, the Club Reward item will also be an epic item or better." Many modules guarantee you at least one "uncommon or better" item. Simply because of RNG, it is possible that the guaranteed "uncommon or better" item gets you a high rarity item in the regular loot but only an uncommon item in the extra chest.
